_about: Brie's moments, observations, Look around words and away lines.
Moments use the same format as content/dialogue (pages, choices, ignore); Brie's name shows on the box. Every moment needs 2 to 5 choices,
Choices are shown in a random order each time. tier and max_tier the same: the moment only happens at that bond level.
and it waits for your answer (the cat stays put). ignore is the quiet choice used only if you leave the café while it's open; it is never shown as an extra choice.
When a moment can happen (all optional): tier (lowest: stranger, curious, familiar, friend, your_cat), max_tier (highest),
when (parts of the day: late night, dawn, morning, afternoon, evening, night), weather (clear, cloudy, drizzle, rain, heavy_rain, fog, snow),
poses (her pose when it starts; left out: awake), spots (where she is),
drink ("any" or a drink id, like cafe_creme), comes_to (she moves to this spot first, if her bond allows it).
What it does: each choice has a bond (how much closer it brings her; can be negative) and a manner (calm or sudden).
then: what she does afterwards (stay, sit, loaf, sleep, leave, away), for the whole moment or for one choice.
Observations are small lines with no choices, shown in Look around when you look at her; text can be a list to pick from. Same conditions as moments.
Keep each page short: about 3 lines of 46 letters at most. An observation plus her look line should fit 4 lines.
look: what you see and can do when you look at her (Esc menu, Look around).
looks: how she looks, by tier (the highest one she has reached is shown). doing: what she's up to, by pose; {where} is her spot in words (content/look.json).
actions: things you can do, each from a tier (curious and up; strangers get none). Same fields as choices (bond, manner, then)
plus reply (what happens, a page or two), poses (her pose; left out: awake), drink, comes_to.
Each cat offers one action each time you look around; after it, the panel ends with a quiet observation about her (one without "you" in it) instead.
rest: shown if you look around again while she is still resting (4 café minutes after an action).
away: what she was like while you were away, for the note when you come back (content/narrator/away.json).
bond: new (stranger or curious), knows (familiar or friend) or yours (your cat). gone: short (under long_from_hours) or long.

calm: Brie tilts her head a little, then goes back to what she was doing.
sudden: Brie gives you a long, cool look, then turns her back on you.
other: Brie considers this carefully, then settles down with a small sigh.

reply: Brie sighs back, a long one, and looks very satisfied with the exchange.
Brie gives a small, put-upon shrug. It's the cushion, apparently. It's always the cushion.

pages: Brie is looking at you. Not at you, exactly. Past you, actually.

reply: Brie turns her head, very slightly, as though she had meant to do that all along.

pages: Brie grooms one of her paws with great care, then another.

pages: Brie closes her eyes slowly, then opens them again.

pages: Brie settles against your arm and starts to purr, very quietly.

pages: Brie walks past your table without looking at you.

pages: Brie sits on the floor and looks at the empty chair across from you. Then at you. Then at the chair.

Brie sighs at the chair, then stays on the floor, slightly offended.
Brie stares at the bag as if it were a personal insult, then sits on the floor again.

pages: A tuft of cream fur drifts past your nose. Across the room, Brie looks innocent.

Brie's ears flick towards the sneeze. She doesn't turn round, but she heard it.

pages: Brie looks at the book on your table, then at you, as if your taste in books were a disappointment.

reply: Brie inspects the cover, sniffs, and looks away, somewhat less disappointed than before.
Brie looks at you for a long time, then names a book in a tone that makes it sound like a sentence.
Brie watches you turn the page, one eyebrow raised, and says nothing.
Brie yawns and sits at the very edge of the table, as far from your book as she can get.

pages: Brie sits on the sill with her back to the room.
She is watching the rain, and she would like everyone to know it.

reply: Brie's tail gives one slow flick. It is, she has decided, a good rain.

choices.text: Ask if she likes the rain

pages: Brie yawns, very slowly, without covering her mouth. She seems to find you boring.

reply: Brie closes her mouth with a snap and looks at you as if you had been rude to the weather.
Brie's eyes narrow. Then she yawns back, very politely, to show she is not impressed.
Brie nods once, as though that settles it. Then she yawns again.

choices.text: Read her a line from your book
reply: Brie listens for one sentence, then gets up and finds a different sunny spot.

pages: Brie lifts her nose. She can smell your café crème from across the room.
She thinks slightly better of you.

reply: Brie comes over, breathes in the steam, and gives a small nod. Small, but a nod.
Brie's ears turn after your sip. She thinks slightly better of you, but she won't say so.

pages: Brie settles by the lamp on the sideboard, in the warmest spot in the room.

Brie gives a short nod, the sort you would give a neighbour on the stairs.

choices.text: Turn the page of your book
reply: Brie watches you turn the page, then goes back to her lamp, satisfied you have been reading.
Brie blinks slowly, then pointedly looks back at the lamp.

pages: Brie's tail swishes once, twice. Something you did has displeased her. You aren't sure what.

reply: Brie's tail stops twitching. That was apparently the right answer, though she won't say so.
Brie gives you a sideways look, then sits up a little straighter herself, which seems to help.
Brie's tail slows, then stops. She decides you are doing well, for now.
Brie's tail thumps the floor once, very loudly, and she walks off without looking back.

pages: Brie walks across the café as if she owned it. To be fair, she might.

reply: Brie gives a regal nod in return, as if you had passed some kind of test.
Brie sniffs and says nothing, but she slows down so you can see her go past.
Brie looks at you very slowly, as though the question were the funniest thing she had heard all week.
Brie stops walking. The silence afterwards is very long and very cold.

pages: Brie's collar has twisted round. She is pretending she hasn't noticed.

reply: Brie lets you fix her collar and holds perfectly still, eyes closed, until you are done.
Brie gives her collar a quick, embarrassed shake. The collar stays exactly as it was.

pages: A patch of sun falls on the sill. Brie moves into it with great dignity, one paw at a time.

reply: Brie lifts her chin and basks in the compliment, very visibly, in the sunlight.

choices.text: Turn your chair to the sun too
reply: Brie gives you an approving glance, then settles deeper into the warm patch.
Brie purrs once, softly, in the sunlight. She clearly appreciates being left to it.

pages: Brie watches you drink. When you put the cup down, she sighs, as if you've done it wrong.

reply: Brie watches you lift the cup with a small, impressed nod. You're improving, she thinks.
Brie gives a theatrical sigh, then shows you the proper way, with one dainty lift of the chin.
Brie shakes her head slowly and turns to watch the window instead.

pages: Brie kneads the cushion in the cat bed for a long time.

choices.text: Tell her it looks very comfortable
reply: Brie pauses in her kneading, looks pleased, and then gets properly comfortable.
Brie's whiskers twitch, and she pretends the cushion was not the joke.
Brie kneads a little longer, then flops down beside the cushion with great dignity.

pages: Brie sneezes. Then she looks around to see if anyone saw.

reply: Brie looks away too, very quickly, and the moment is over before it began.
Brie's ears flatten, pleased, and she says something that sounds rather like thank you.

choices.text: Sneeze too, to keep her company
reply: Brie stares at you, then sneezes again herself, as if you had started it.
Brie's tail stiffens, and she walks off with her nose in the air.

pages: Brie has come close enough to read over your shoulder. She doesn't think much of the chapter.

reply: Brie watches the page turn with approval, then leans in to read the next one.
Brie listens to the line, then corrects your pronunciation without looking up.

choices.text: Hold the book a little lower
reply: Brie settles at your feet, reading over the edge, and seems quite content with that.

pages: The rain is so loud that Brie flattens her ears.
She glares at the window as if it were being rude on purpose.

reply: Her glare and yours meet in the glass. She looks, very briefly, like an ally.
Brie watches the curtain slide across, then purrs softly. Somebody has finally listened.
Brie glances at you, unconvinced, but she doesn't argue. The rain goes on.

pages: Brie stretches, front paws far ahead, back legs far behind. It takes a while. Everybody waits.

reply: Brie gives you a look of deep approval and stretches again, a little longer this time.
Brie takes a bow from the top of her stretch. The café pays attention.

pages: Brie sits as close as she dares to your café crème and looks at the ceiling, as if the cup weren't there.

reply: Brie leans in, sniffs the foam, and makes a small noise of pure contentment.

choices.text: Tell her it's very good today
reply: Brie's eyes slide to the cup. She lets out a long, thoughtful breath, and nods.
Brie keeps her eyes on the ceiling, and her tail quietly stops twitching.

choices.text: Pull the cup closer to you
reply: Brie gives the cup a wounded glance, then sits down with her back to you.

pages: Brie lies by the lamp with her paws tucked in.
Every few minutes she lets out a small sigh, to remind the room she's there.

reply: Brie's sigh is answered with another, and this time she sounds almost content.
Brie opens one eye and considers the question for a long time, then closes it again.
Brie's tail lifts, very slightly, in reply. Goodnight, it seems, is acceptable.

pages: Brie jumps onto the chair across from you and sits as if she had a reservation.

reply: Brie gives you a knowing look, the kind you give someone who has always ordered the same thing.

pages: Brie licks a paw and smooths down a bit of fur on her forehead. She looks at you to check it worked.

pages: Brie sits on the sill and moves over, a little, as if someone might want to join her.

Brie points her nose at a chimney pot across the way. That, apparently, is what she is looking at.

pages: Brie flops onto her side with a heavy sigh, as if the whole day had been too much.

pages: Your bookmark has fallen on the floor. Brie is sitting next to it, looking innocent.

pages: Brie watches the snow fall past the window.

choices.text: Tell her it matches her fur

pages: Brie sits by the lamp on the sideboard. In its light her fur looks almost gold. She knows.

pages: Brie has found a sugar cube on the floor.

reply: Brie stretches under your hand and rolls onto her back across the page, purring.

pages: Brie sits beside your cup and watches every sip go by, very seriously.
